methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $235M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero, a Series B transportation company founded by John Langford, has raised $235M to date. The broader Transportation sector comp universe consists of 7 private peers (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and The ePlane Company) with no direct public comparables.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: Stage-Progression. This approach applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $235M total raised proxy, reflecting typical Series B advancement economics, yielding an implied valuation of $446M. A Peer-Median method was not applicable; while 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, none satisfied narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier matching. Constructing a reliable median from the broader peer set risked introducing distortion.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $380M (low) to $513M (high), with a median point of $446M. The width of this range reflects reliance on a single method, creating material methodological uncertainty. Confidence is further constrained by the absence of public comps and the limited applicability of peer-based cross-checks within the Transportation frontier-tech segment. Resolution of valuation would benefit from either tighter peer comparability data or forward-looking milestones (funding round pricing, revenue multiples, or capital efficiency metrics) that could anchor additional triangulation methods.
